title: Inducing Group Fairness in Prompt-Based Language Model Decisions
findings: Prompted Language Model classifiers demonstrated significant unfairness, with comments related to Muslim and Jewish groups having 89% and 48% higher False Positive Rates (FPR) for toxicity, respectively, compared to the Christian group. Embedding-based classifiers showed even larger gaps (124% for Muslim, 71% for Jewish). Regularization-based remediation techniques were more effective at improving fairness than prompt-based methods, which failed to significantly decrease the FPR gap.
